_note: v2 hook overrides for la tente du Concours (B54_concours). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace hooks that differ from what is painted (nothing may be written in the paintings).

fr_meme_adj.hook: "MEHM": two framed cat MEMES, exactly the SAME picture. même = same.
fr_meme_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows two sheep in matching hats and rosettes (not goats munching a rosette).

fr_excellent_adj.hook: Like English 'excellent', said ayk-seh-LAHN: a judge pins a blue rosette on a giant cabbage and declares it EXCELLENT, nasal on the end.
fr_excellent_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the prize vegetable painted is a cabbage, not a pumpkin.

fr_parfait_adj.hook: A PERFECT ice-cream parfait with a cherry on top earns ten out of ten: the judge holds up all ten fingers.
fr_parfait_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the judge's raised hands that are painted beside the parfait.

fr_formidable_adj.hook: Not 'formidable' in the English sense: formidable (for-mee-DAHBL) means GREAT, FANTASTIC; a grandma gives a big thumbs-up beside a perfect pink cake.
fr_formidable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a grandma with a thumbs-up by the pink cake rather than a judge.

fr_superbe_adj.hook: Like English 'superb', said sew-PEHRB: a bumblebee wears a SUPERB rosette, "SUPER, B!", and loops the tent in joy.
fr_superbe_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted bee already wears the rosette; no judge is shown handing it over.

fr_fantastique_adj.hook: Like English 'fantastic', said fahn-tahs-TEEK: a FANTASTIC giant pumpkin grins beside its golden trophy, blushing orange.
fr_fantastique_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the trophy painted is a golden cup, not a carved teak one.

fr_sympa_adj.hook: Like English 'sympathetic', said san-PAH: kindly grandad SAM, PA to everyone, pours lemonade for each nervous entrant: so NICE.
fr_sympa_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted grandad pouring lemonade into glasses.

fr_pareil_adj.hook: Two twins march in a PARADE ("pah-REHY") with matching drums, wearing exactly the SAME costume.
fr_pareil_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted twins are drummers. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (pa-RAY) -> (pah-REHY) to match the card.

fr_important_adj.hook: Like English 'important', said an-por-TAHN: an ANT carries a medal almost her own size up the stand, very IMPORTANT.
fr_important_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted ant carries a medal; there is no sash.

fr_grave_adj.hook: Like English 'grave', said GRAHV: a SERIOUS owl judge in a cap peers through her spectacles at a jam jar, feathers bristling.
fr_grave_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted owl holding the jam jar.

fr_normal_adj.hook: Like English 'normal', said nor-MAHL: a perfectly NORMAL little tomato sits beside a giant one, looking embarrassed.
fr_normal_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the giant one is painted as a big tomato, not a pumpkin.

fr_serieux_adj.hook: Like English 'serious', said say-RYEUH: a SERIOUS hedgehog judge examines a diamond through a magnifying glass, a carrot at her feet.
fr_serieux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a hedgehog with a magnifier and a diamond beside a carrot.

fr_pire_adj.hook: Things get WORSE and WORSE: a toy pier ("PIER") sinks plank by plank into a washtub.
fr_pire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the pier is painted as a toy in a washtub on the stand.

fr_inutile_adj.hook: Like English 'inutile', said ee-new-TEEL: a NEW TEAL umbrella full of holes is USELESS, and the little mouse under it stands dripping.
fr_inutile_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted figure under the holey teal umbrella is a mouse.

fr_necessaire_adj.hook: Like English 'necessary', said nay-say-SEHR: a pony shakes its head "NAY!" but the rabbit judge holds up a ticket and SAYS it is NECESSARY.
fr_necessaire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted judge is a rabbit holding a ticket beside a pony.

fr_double_adj.hook: Like English 'double', said DOOBL: a mouse chef presents a DOUBLE cake, two tiers balanced on a stand, "doobly-doo!"
fr_double_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted chef with the two-tier cake.

fr_reel_adj.hook: Like English 'real', said ray-EHL: a badger judge checks a stingray in a tank to see if it's REAL, and RAY yells "ELL!"
fr_reel_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a badger peering at a stingray in a glass tank.

fr_nul_adj.hook: A RUBBISH, useless entry: a mouse judge drops a wilted lettuce into the crate and scores it NIL, null.
fr_nul_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a mouse judge dropping a limp lettuce; nothing written, so no scoreboard.

fr_utile_adj.hook: Like English 'utility', said ew-TEEL: a fox girl holds up a teal pocket knife, the most USEFUL thing in the tent: "YOU, TEAL, you saved us!"
fr_utile_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted fox girl with the teal knife.

fr_vain_adj.hook: A VAIN peacock sits in a toy van ("VAN") admiring his own portrait in a gilded frame.
fr_vain_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a peacock in a van beside a framed mirror portrait.

fr_innocent_adj.hook: Like English 'innocent', said ee-noh-SAHN: a puppy sits IN NO SUN, looking INNOCENT beside a chewed slipper.
fr_innocent_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted puppy and slipper.

fr_prive_adj.hook: Like English 'private', said pree-VAY: a cat naps in her PRIVATE corner of the stand, her blue rosette pinned beside her: do not disturb.
fr_prive_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted cat naps beside a rosette; no ribbon barrier is painted.

fr_ideal_adj.hook: Like English 'ideal', said ee-day-AHL: two pigs hold the IDEAL marrow between them and shake on "A DEAL".
fr_ideal_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows two pigs sharing the marrow (no judge).

fr_chouette_adj.hook: An owl (une chouette) gives a thumbs-up from the top of the stand: "COOL! GREAT!"
fr_chouette_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: no mouse is being shooed in the painting.

fr_majeur_adj.hook: Like English 'major', said mah-ZHUHR: a MAJOR prize, a trophy taller than a mouse, goes to the smallest pumpkin.
fr_majeur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted gold trophy, mouse and little pumpkin.

fr_digne_adj.hook: Like English 'dignified', said DEENY: a DEAN in cap and gown is WORTHY of the rosette and holds it with dignity.
fr_digne_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted dean holds the rosette rather than bowing.

fr_suffisant_adj.hook: Like English 'sufficient', said sew-fee-ZAHN: one small apple is SUFFICIENT for two mice to share.
fr_suffisant_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: two mice are painted sharing the apple.

fr_legitime_adj.hook: Like English 'legitimate', said lay-zhee-TEEM: the judging TEAM inspect the giant marrow with a magnifier: LEGITIMATE, not a painted balloon.
fr_legitime_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted judges and magnifier.

fr_connu_adj.hook: A FAMOUS knight on a gnu ("NU") rides by, and everyone KNOWS him: the onlookers wave.
fr_connu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the painted onlookers.

fr_splendide_adj.hook: Like English 'splendid', said splahn-DEED: a grandma pins a SPLENDID rosette on the boy whose good DEED was carrying everyone's pies.
fr_splendide_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted boy with a stack of pies and the grandma's rosette.

fr_remarquable_adj.hook: Like English 'remarkable', said ruh-mahr-KAHBL: a REMARKABLE carrot at the show is shaped exactly like a rabbit, and the real rabbit beside it is offended.
fr_remarquable_adj.why: kept, clarified to the painted pair.

fr_exceptionnel_adj.hook: Like English 'exceptional', said ehk-sehp-syoh-NEHL: NELL waters her EXCEPTIONAL sunflower, which grows right through the tent roof.
fr_exceptionnel_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds Nell's watering can as painted.

fr_inattendu_adj.hook: An UNEXPECTED guest, a giraffe, pokes its head into the tent ("ee-nah-tahn-DEW") through the roof.
fr_inattendu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the giraffe peeps in through the roof opening. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ee-na-ton-DU -> ee-nah-tahn-DEW).

fr_singulier_adj.hook: Like English 'singular', said san-gew-LYAY: a SINGULAR entry at the show: a GULL that sings opera, and the judges shout "YAY!"
fr_singulier_adj.why: kept: the painting shows the gull and cheering judges.

fr_negatif_adj.hook: Like English 'negative', said nay-gah-TEEF: a grumpy pony judge frowns at a row of cupcakes and gives them all a NEGATIVE score: "NAY!"
fr_negatif_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted pony judges cupcakes.

fr_injuste_adj.hook: Like English 'unjust', said an-ZHEWST: a goat has grabbed the judge's rosette, and the judge clutches his cheeks: UNJUST!
fr_injuste_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted goat wears the rosette beside the shocked judge.

fr_indispensable_adj.hook: Like English 'indispensable', said an-dees-pahn-SAHBL: a judge's INDISPENSABLE tool: a magnifying glass almost as big as his head.
fr_indispensable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted magnifier.

fr_inoubliable_adj.hook: An elephant never forgets an UNFORGETTABLE ("ee-noo-blee-YAHBL") party cake bristling with candles.
fr_inoubliable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted elephant and candle cake.

fr_insupportable_adj.hook: Like English 'insupportable', said an-sew-por-TAHBL: a little table sags under a pumpkin so heavy the weight is UNBEARABLE.
fr_insupportable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted table and pumpkin.

fr_atroce_adj.hook: Like English 'atrocious', said ah-TROS: ROSS's soup is so ATROCIOUS that the judge winces at his spoon and the tent dog backs away.
fr_atroce_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the spoon is not bent in the painting.

fr_cense_adj.hook: A boy is SUPPOSED TO be tidying the cake tins, but the SON SAYS ("sahn-SAY") "Five more minutes!", holding up five fingers from under the pile.
fr_cense_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted pile is cake tins, with the boy's five raised fingers. Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (son-SAY) -> (sahn-SAY) to match the card.

fr_satisfaisant_adj.hook: Like English 'satisfying', said sah-tees-fuh-ZAHN: a SATISFYING crack as the judge taps the top of a perfect crème brûlée.

fr_moqueur_adj.hook: A MOCKING mockingbird ("moh-KUHR") copies the tiny judge's pose and laughs.
fr_moqueur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted bird mimics a small judge.

fr_insuffisant_adj.hook: Like English 'insufficient', said an-sew-fee-ZAHN: an INSUFFICIENT slice of cake for a whale in her tub, who stares at it sadly.
fr_insuffisant_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the whale is painted in a tub.

fr_acceptable_adj.hook: Like English 'acceptable', said ahk-sehp-TAHBL: the hedgehog judge shrugs at a lumpy green dish: ACCEPTABLE.
fr_acceptable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted dish is a lumpy green jelly, not a marrow.

fr_adequat_adj.hook: Like English 'adequate', said ah-day-KWAH: a duck judges her washtub ADEQUATE for a swim, "QUACK," and settles her feathers.
fr_adequat_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the duck sits in a tub, not a pond.

fr_inacceptable_adj.hook: Like English 'unacceptable', said ee-nahk-sehp-TAHBL: a judge holds up a moldy pie: UNACCEPTABLE, and the flies agree.

fr_tenu_adj.hook: Like English 'tenuous', said tay-NEW: the prize waistcoat's new buttons hang on by THIN, TENUOUS loose threads, about to snap.
fr_tenu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows a waistcoat with loose threads.

fr_reve_adj.hook: A dreamy reverie ("ray-VAY"): a judge dozing in his armchair dreams of a PERFECT, IDEAL beach (rêve).
fr_reve_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dream beach floats in a bubble over a dozing judge.

fr_incontournable_adj.hook: A giant marrow statue stands in the middle of the rug and the judges can't get round it ("in-con-TOUR-nable"): UNMISSABLE.
fr_incontournable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted statue is a marrow on the rug with judges walking round.

fr_inadmissible_adj.hook: Like English 'inadmissible', said ee-nahd-mee-SEEBL: an UNACCEPTABLE entry: a cake made of mud, and only the piglet beside it is pleased.
fr_inadmissible_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the painted piglet.

fr_indique_adj.hook: A signpost points: "As INDICATED!" ("an-dee-KAY"): just the RIGHT, APPROPRIATE way to go, and a snail follows it.
fr_indique_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the painted snail; the signpost is blank.

fr_facheux_adj.hook: An ANNOYING pebble in a fancy shoe ("fah-SHEUH"): the lady in the flowered hat shakes it out, unfortunate and irritating.
fr_facheux_adj.why: kept, clarified to the painted lady.

fr_imprevu_adj.hook: UNEXPECTED ("an-pray-VEW"): a jack-in-the-box bursts out with streamers, a view no one had previewed, and the kitten leaps back.
fr_imprevu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the surprise is painted as a jack-in-the-box, not a party.

fr_infect_adj.hook: IN FACT ("an-FEHKT") the soup is VILE: green and steaming with stink, and even the fly holds its nose.
fr_infect_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted soup is green and stinky; no mold.

fr_septieme_adj.hook: Is that the SEVENTH ("seh-TYEHM")? A judge mouse counts the big ladybird's spots and points at the SEVENTH.
fr_septieme_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the seventh place is painted as a seven-spot ladybird (nothing may be written, so no number 7).

fr_catastrophique_adj.hook: Like English 'catastrophic', said kah-tahs-troh-FEEK: a CATASTROPHIC cake: the tiers slide sideways and the little chef topper dives for safety.
fr_catastrophique_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted cake topper is a chef, not a bride.

fr_huitieme_adj.hook: A wee team ("wee-TYEHM") of eight arms: the octopus player counts them and waves the EIGHTH high.
fr_huitieme_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the eight are painted as an octopus's arms (no written 8). Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (wee-TYEM -> wee-TYEHM).

fr_fantaisiste_adj.hook: Like English 'fantasist', said fahn-tay-ZEEST: a FANCIFUL marrow carved into a little dragon wins a special ribbon.

fr_fiable_adj.hook: In the old fable ("FYAHBL") the slow but RELIABLE, DEPENDABLE tortoise plods on and always arrives, the storybook lying open beside him.

fr_prometteur_adj.hook: Said proh-meh-TUHR: a PROMISING little seedling sprouts in its pot, one to watch.
fr_prometteur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the seedling is painted in a small pot, with no ribbon. Text pass 2026-10-28: removed 'Like English X' (not a cognate).

fr_significatif_adj.hook: Like English 'significant', said see-nyee-fee-kah-TEEF: a SIGNIFICANT moment: the judge tastes the jam, pauses, and smiles.

fr_notable_adj.hook: Like English 'notable', said noh-TAHBL: a NOTABLE entry: a carrot-headed lookalike stands beside the judge, nose and all.
fr_notable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painting shows the carrot-faced lookalike next to the judge.

fr_souhaitable_adj.hook: At the party the sweet table ("sweh-TAHBL") is the most DESIRABLE spot: the children wish (souhaitent) to stay right beside it.
fr_souhaitable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: two children are painted at the table.

fr_prenant_adj.hook: A prawn clings on ("pruh-NAHN") to a GRIPPING, CAPTIVATING storybook, unable to put it down.

fr_experimente_adj.hook: Like English 'experienced', said ehk-spay-ree-mahn-TAY: an EXPERIENCED judge, an old tortoise in spectacles, has tasted jam for a hundred years.

fr_prioritaire_adj.hook: Like English 'priority', said pree-yoh-ree-TEHR: a PRIORITY lane for snails, marked out with little flags.
fr_prioritaire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the painted flags.

fr_pertinent_adj.hook: Like English 'pertinent', said pehr-tee-NAHN: a mouse beside a cheese asks a PERTINENT question: "Where is the cheese category?"
fr_pertinent_adj.why: kept, clarified to the painted mouse and cheese.

fr_reparateur_adj.hook: A REPAIR shop ("ray-pah-rah-TUHR") where a nap is RESTORATIVE: a teddy snoozes under a quilt among shining mended toys.
fr_reparateur_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted teddy and toys. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ray-pa-ra-TUHR -> ray-pah-rah-TUHR).

fr_performant_adj.hook: Like English 'performant', said pehr-for-MAHN: an EFFICIENT robot peels a mountain of potatoes in seconds.

fr_inoffensif_adj.hook: Like English 'inoffensive', said ee-noh-fahn-SEEF: a HARMLESS grass snake curls up under a straw sun hat for a nap.
fr_inoffensif_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the snake is painted under the hat.

fr_avantageux_adj.hook: Like English 'advantageous', said ah-vahn-tah-ZHEUH: an ADVANTAGEOUS spot for the little vegetable van, parked right by the tent door.

fr_nefaste_adj.hook: A horse shakes his head "Neigh!" at a greasy fast-food ("nay-FAHST") burger, HARMFUL to his health.
fr_nefaste_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the carrot is not painted; the horse and burger are. Example sentence replaced: the source example was about tobacco.
ex: La friture est néfaste pour la santé.
Fried food is harmful to health.

fr_benefique_adj.hook: Like English 'beneficial', said bay-nay-FEEK: BENEFICIAL rain falls only on the prize roses, from one obliging little cloud.

fr_usage_adj.hook: A shoe so USED and WORN ("ew-zah-ZHAY") from heavy usage that its toes peek out and the sole flaps.
fr_usage_adj.why: kept, matches the painting. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ew-za-ZHAY -> ew-zah-ZHAY).

fr_salutaire_adj.hook: Like English 'salutary', said sah-lew-TEHR: a SALUTARY walk: the dog comes back fitter and smiling, lead trailing.
fr_salutaire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dog is painted alone with its lead.

fr_hasardeux_adj.hook: Like English 'hazardous', said ah-zahr-DEUH: a RISKY leap: a goat jumps off a little table past a wobbly chair.
fr_hasardeux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: matches the painted goat, table and chair.

fr_nocif_adj.hook: Like English 'noxious', said noh-SEEF: HARMFUL black fumes from a burnt pie make the judge cough.
fr_nocif_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted pie gives off fumes rather than just being black.

fr_preventif_adj.hook: Like English 'preventive', said pray-vahn-TEEF: a PREVENTIVE umbrella opened by a cautious hedgehog under a clear sunny sky.

fr_vieillot_adj.hook: Grandpa's QUAINT, OLD-FASHIONED wooden yo-yo ("vyeh-YOH"), painted with faded flowers, rests beside his pocket watch.

fr_degradant_adj.hook: Like English 'degrading', said day-grah-DAHN: a DEGRADING costume: a proud lion forced to wear bunny ears.

fr_illicite_adj.hook: Like English 'illicit', said ee-lee-SEET: an ILLICIT snack: a dog hides under a LILY-flowered SEAT cushion, sausages peeking out.
fr_illicite_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dog is painted hiding with the sausages under the cushion.

fr_decisif_adj.hook: Like English 'decisive', said day-see-ZEEF: a DECISIVE judge takes one bite of pie and rings his bell at once: winner.
fr_decisif_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cubby shows the judge mid-bite ringing a hand bell.

fr_poli_adj.hook: Like English 'polite', said poh-LEE: Polly the parrot bows to the prize marrow, wing on her chest, ever so POLITE.
fr_poli_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cubby shows the parrot bowing to one marrow; the wiping of feet and the judges are not painted.

fr_rassurant_adj.hook: Like English 'reassuring', said rah-sew-RAHN: RON the old judge gives a REASSURING smile and a pat to a nervous little girl holding her first jam jar.
fr_rassurant_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the pat on the shoulder that is painted.

fr_recu_adj.hook: Sue ("ruh-SEW") is handed her parcel and a little paper slip: the parcel is RECEIVED, and the slip is a reçu, a RECEIPT.
fr_recu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the shopkeeper hands over both the parcel and the (blank) receipt slip in the cubby. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (ruh-SU -> ruh-SEW).

fr_somptueux_adj.hook: Like English 'sumptuous', said sohnp-TWEUH: a SUMPTUOUS tiered white cake with two sugar swans on top.
fr_somptueux_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the painted cake has three tiers and two swans, not seven tiers.

fr_vital_adj.hook: Like English 'vital', said vee-TAHL: a TALL glass of water is VITAL for the red-faced judge after tasting the fiery chillies.

fr_decu_adj.hook: A DISAPPOINTED girl called Sue ("day-SEW") in her party hat holds the string of a popped balloon.
fr_decu_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the party hat that is painted; the cubby shows only the girl, not the party. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (day-SU -> day-SEW).

fr_impeccable_adj.hook: Like English 'impeccable', said an-pay-KAHBL: a hen in a bow tie with IMPECCABLE manners PECKS politely at the prize pie, one crumb at a time.
fr_impeccable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: adds the painted bow tie.

fr_infernal_adj.hook: Like English 'infernal', said an-fehr-NAHL: an INFERNAL heat fills the tent, so two sweating judges fan themselves with giant FERN leaves.
fr_infernal_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: two judges are painted, sweating.

fr_precaire_adj.hook: Like English 'precarious', said pray-KEHR: a PRECARIOUS tower of marmalade jars wobbles on a little table, and a mouse tiptoes past with great CARE.
fr_precaire_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: a mouse, not 'everyone', tiptoes past in the cubby, and the jars are on a little table.

fr_typique_adj.hook: Like English 'typical', said tee-PEAK: a TYPICAL cat lifts the tablecloth to PEEK underneath at a dropped blob of cream.
fr_typique_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cat lifts a checked cloth over a blob of cream on the floor.

fr_epouvantable_adj.hook: Listen for VAN and TABLE in it: a delivery VAN tips its honey pots all over the cake TABLE: an APPALLING, AWFUL sticky mess.
fr_epouvantable_adj.why: Reworded to match the painting: the source hook named a cartoon character and a crude sound-alike; the painting shows a plain van spilling honey on a cake table.
